fix(renderer): a frame's hold is released when its view's request throws (ibyq.at1)

A frame's setup reads the held view's request inside the scope that
releases the hold, so a throw from that read no longer strands it and
keeps a retired state from being reclaimed.

The lane derivation's read of the last returned plan is marked as the
exception it is: an input MobX cannot see, written only by the
declaration that returns this derivation's output. Its header says where
each switch comes from. The frame path's files (render cache, draw,
session source and state, feeds, render payload) carry reasons in place
of ticket ids.

test(renderer): a still frame hands back the declaration the host follows (ibyq.at1)

Across still due frames, the renderer returns the very subscriptions
object the host already follows. The view-hold spy now has a positive
control: the drawn session is held, and the other session never is.

The frame path's comments give reasons, not ticket ids. The view door's
comment names both of its readers, and the reload comment says that the
next frame draws the successor or its opening's failure. The lane
derivation's untracked read of the last returned plan states why it
needs no tracking.

test(renderer): a still frame touches only the view it draws (ibyq.at1)

Across still due frames with two live sessions, the session that is not
drawn has its view held by nothing, beside the existing checks that the
subscription, origin and session reads are not repeated. A walk over
every view's hold injected into the per-turn declaration fails it.

The render cache's frame-path comments give their reasons without
ticket ids.

test(renderer): use explicit session inputs and bind samples once (#905)

Host and renderer tests run on the production daemon with explicit session inputs, and fixture draws bind their sample once, as a session binds its view.

- Sessions report only what they declare: the worker's PATH and an empty Claude directory.
- A test file's fixture launchers belong to its runtime, and the test environment ends them after the file's last hook. An integration test checks this across two files in one process. The runner's global teardown reads the process table through its own probe.
- Prepared configs resolve their globals over their own user file's authored preset roots, through the daemon's derivation.
- The pane-subscribe hang-up, the click's mailbox wait and the absent user layer are each pinned against real behaviour.

Four law-review passes; triage is recorded on the PR and on candybar-law-review-ibyq.xrv. Follow-ups are filed in the epic as .s4k (watch join window) and .6zj (launcher lifetime required).

fix(config): one key classifier, one write router, and Back steps that end with their edit

What a session key is (edit mode's own, a setting, a confirm, the
viewer, a menu, an author's) is decided by one function, and every
reader and writer switches on it. Every session write passes one
router: an open edit holds it, and with none open edit mode's keys are
set aside for the edit a click opens, or dropped and logged. An edit
holds the Back steps taken in it, and the click that ends it lands its
own step outside, without edit mode's keys. Whether an edit has work is
the files it changed and the drafts a save writes, one count for the
save cell, cancel and the idle close. The duplicate-id hint is fixed
text, the click error reads only records this build writes, and a
session left empty by the load takes no slot.

fix(config): decide edit-or-store once per click and check authored keys wherever they load

A click outside an edit holds edit mode's keys aside: they open the edit
it starts, or are dropped and logged at warn. Every reader takes the
edit's view, the main undo never records an edit key, and drafts are
neither main-undo nor navigation state. A closed edit's steps are never
Back destinations because its state never reaches the store.

The authored-key check runs for plugins too, refuses raw keys by
namespace and accordion keys only where they meet the bar's own. The
click error lives under the settings namespace. Hover text decodes menu
keys. Minted placement ids retry a bounded number of times and throw.
fix(config): give re-added placements a fresh id and keep edit-mode state in the edit

fix(settings): fold every pick through one setting table and warn on stale picks

A session pick its setting can no longer hold (an uninstalled or retired theme, an undeclared style or preset, a dropped effect, an out-of-range value, a placement value outside its declaration) now reads through its setting's one parse as stale. The fold draws what lies beneath it and reports which rung decided, and the frame shows one stale warning per stale pick that decided, naming the setting, the spelling held, what the bar wears and what the setting can hold. Every save releases every pick that is not a draft against the config it wrote, and a state variable may no longer read a setting's session key.
